attrs.gap: OPEN, AND NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Fable proposed a seven-node six-edge vocabulary and argued sufficiency from a literature comparison; GPT-5.6 refused to freeze it on that basis and named the removal test. scripts/asr-min-graph.mjs blinds one type at a time and re-runs the real gate. 12 of 13 types are load-bearing — their removal costs at least one registered refusal. `field:Disposition` is descriptive only: removing every stored sustained/terminated disposition fails 2 checks and loses no refusal, which is correct, because a disposition is an input to the derivation and not a gate. `edge:AppliesUnder` scored ZERO ON BOTH and that finding is now MOS-APPLIESUNDER-CLOSED. WHAT THE TEST DOES NOT SHOW, and why this record stays open: that no SMALLER vocabulary encodes the same refusals differently. Each type is used; whether two could be one is the actual minimality question.
